post-aqft-smeft-model.physical_scope: An adopted, formal, linearly realized Standard Model effective-operator model on the trivial four-dimensional Minkowski bundle, through canonical dimension six. It supplies no functional measure, continuum construction, ultraviolet completion, measured coefficient, or claim that the postulate describes nature.

post-aqft-smeft-model:
## Postulate

Adopt four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for engineering dimensions, so $\partial_\mu$ has mass dimension one, a scalar field has dimension one, a spinor field has dimension $3/2$, and a gauge field strength has dimension two.

The gauge group is the direct product $G_{\mathrm{SM}}=SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, with this global form and not a quotient by a subgroup of its center. Write an element of $U(1)_Y$ as $z\in U(1)$ and normalize its integer charge as $y=6Y$, so its representation acts by $z^y$. The three-family matter fields and scalar are smooth fields in the representations
$$q_L:(3,2)_1,\qquad u_R:(3,1)_4,\qquad d_R:(3,1)_{-2},\qquad \ell_L:(1,2)_{-3},\qquad e_R:(1,1)_{-6},\qquad H:(1,2)_3.$$
There are no right-handed neutrino fields. Fermion components are Grassmann odd; $H$ is a Grassmann-even complex doublet. The global charges are $B(q_L)=B(u_R)=B(d_R)=1/3$, $L(\ell_L)=L(e_R)=1$, and zero for $H$ and the gauge fields; the corresponding $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ transformations multiply each field by the phase determined by its charge. Impose these as exact selection rules on the retained formal local interactions; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. There is no flavor symmetry beyond the displayed gauge action: Yukawa and Wilson coefficients may carry unrestricted three-family indices subject to the stated reality and Hermitian-conjugation conditions.

Choose a reference symmetry-breaking radius $v>0$ of mass dimension one. If it is interpreted as a vacuum radius, the supplied scalar-potential coefficients are assumed to make $H^\dagger H=v^2/2$ a local minimum; this postulate does not derive that parameter constraint. Define $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, where $\sigma^2$ is the second Pauli matrix.

Choose the trivial smooth right principal bundle $P=M\times G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ and only this bundle sector. A connection is a smooth right-principal connection with the convention $\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$. In a local section, a field in representation $\rho$ has covariant derivative $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_*(A_\mu)$, and the gauge curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$ with the graded-bracket convention of the supplied gauge-geometry data. The ordinary component hypercharges are $Y=y/6$; in particular $Y(H)=1/2$. The formal local interaction set imposes the exact $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ selection rules stated above; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. Yukawa matrices are otherwise arbitrary.

The adopted object is a formal local Lagrangian density made from finitely many fields, covariant derivatives, and field strengths at one spacetime point, contracted to Lorentz scalars and invariant under the stated gauge and global actions. The renormalizable part has the gauge kinetic terms $-\tfrac14G^A_{\mu\nu}G^{A\mu\nu}-\tfrac14W^I_{\mu\nu}W^{I\mu\nu}-\tfrac14B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu}$, fermion kinetic terms $i\sum_\psi\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi$, Higgs kinetic term $-(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H$, the real gauge-invariant Higgs potential
$$V_4(H)=V_0-\mu_H^2H^\dagger H+\lambda(H^\dagger H)^2,\qquad V_0,\mu_H^2,\lambda\in\mathbb R,$$
and Yukawa terms
$$-\left(\bar q_LY_dHd_R+\bar q_LY_u\widetilde H u_R+\bar\ell_LY_eHe_R+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$
where each $Y_f$ is a complex $3\times3$ family matrix and h.c. is the Hermitian conjugate. Set the gauge theta terms to zero in this selected model. Add finite sets $I_d$ of local gauge-invariant, $B$- and $L$-neutral polynomial operators $\mathcal O_{d,i}$ at each retained dimension $d\leq6$. Retain derivative-jet order at most two, maximum polynomial field degree six, and loop order zero. Use $C_{d,i}\mathcal O_{d,i}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{d-4}$, where $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ has mass dimension one and each $C_{d,i}$ is dimensionless. The dimension-five set is empty under the adopted exact lepton-number symmetry. The dimension-six set is fixed by the separate Warsaw coefficient contract. Wilson coefficients are supplied parameters, not calculated or fitted here.

This is an operator-level model on smooth fields and compactly supported variations; total divergences are therefore zero in the associated action comparison. Its low-energy use is restricted to external momenta small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, with the finite dimension-six truncation understood formally and without a numerical remainder bound. No regulator or functional measure is adopted, and no finite graph cutoff is identified with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$. The postulate asserts no path integral, continuum limit, ultraviolet completion, or empirical realization.

post-aqft-heft-model.physical_scope: An adopted nonlinear electroweak EFT field realization with a group-valued Goldstone field and an independent scalar singlet, sharing the stated Standard Model gauge and matter data. It supplies no path-integral measure, ultraviolet completion, continuum construction, measured coefficient, or claim that the postulate describes nature.

post-aqft-heft-model:
## Postulate

Use the same four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, direct-product global gauge group, gauge connection, fermion representations, family content, and the preceding model's exact baryon- and lepton-number selection rules on formal local interactions. No anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. In particular, the hypercharge-one-half Higgs doublet of that model is replaced in this realization by three angular Goldstone coordinates and a real scalar singlet; this is a distinct adopted model interface, not a deduction that the two models have identical field spaces.

Let $J=(-v,\infty)$, where $v>0$ is the mass-one reference radius from the preceding model. A scalar field is a smooth map $h:M\to J$ and is invariant under the electroweak gauge group. The Goldstone field is a smooth map $U:M\to SU(2)$, with $SU(2)$ represented by its defining $2\times2$ unitary matrices of determinant one. For an electroweak transformation $g_L(x)\in SU(2)_L$ and $z(x)\in U(1)_Y$, set
$$g_R(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3}),\qquad U(x)\longmapsto g_L(x)U(x)g_R(z(x))^{-1},\qquad h(x)\longmapsto h(x).$$
Thus the left factor is the linearly represented $SU(2)_L$ gauge action, the right factor is the embedded hypercharge action, and $h$ is a gauge singlet. With $T_a=\sigma_a/2$ for the Pauli matrices, the exponential chart
$$U(\pi)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2i\pi^aT_a}{v}\right),\qquad \pi\in\mathbb R^3,\quad \|\pi\|<\pi v,$$
is a smooth coordinate chart near the identity; $U$ itself is the globally valued group field and is not identified with one global exponential-coordinate chart.

Write $W_\mu=W_\mu^aT_a$ and use the local covariant derivative
$$D_\mu U=\partial_\mu U+i g W_\mu U-i g' B_\mu U T_3,$$
with dimensionless gauge couplings $g,g'$ and the same right-principal connection convention as the shared gauge data. The adopted two-derivative scalar density is
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{(2)}=-\frac12K(h)\,\partial_\mu h\,\partial^\mu h-\frac{v^2}{4}F_C(h)\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((D_\mu U)^\dagger D^\mu U\right)-V(h),$$
where $K$ and $F_C$ are supplied smooth real dimensionless functions on $J$, $K(h)>0$ and $F_C(h)>0$ on the field range used, $K(0)=F_C(0)=1$, and $V$ is a supplied real smooth potential of mass dimension four with $V'(0)=0$. Higher local interactions may use smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$, the same gauge and matter fields, covariant derivatives, and curvature tensors, with B and L conserved. This statement adopts no finite derivative or chiral truncation; the separate power-counting definition specifies those cutoffs.

The independent HEFT cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$, the radius $v$, the SMEFT coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, and any finite-regulator cutoff are separate data; no equality or hierarchy among them is imposed here. The model is used only for external energies below its supplied range of validity. It adopts no functional measure or regulator and implies no path integral, ultraviolet completion, infinite-volume limit, or empirical realization.

def-aqft-warsaw-basis-contract.physical_scope: A finite, source-defined dimension-six coefficient convention for the stated three-family, B- and L-conserving SMEFT field content. It does not locally prove the complete Warsaw classification or identify the formal algebraic quotient with every physical compact-group invariant.

def-aqft-warsaw-basis-contract:
## Definition

Use the fields, direct-product gauge group, hypercharge normalization, three-family content, exact $U(1)_B\times U(1)_L$ symmetries, natural units and coefficient scale of the preceding linearly realized model. A local operator is a finite polynomial in these fields and their covariant derivatives at one spacetime point, with all Lorentz, gauge and family indices contracted to a Lorentz and gauge scalar. Its canonical dimension assigns one to $H$ and each derivative, $3/2$ to a fermion, and two to a field strength.

The **Warsaw coefficient contract** is the finite dimension-six source list of gauge-invariant representatives $Q_i^{(6)}$ in Tables 2 and 3 of Grzadkowski, Iskrzynski, Misiak and Rosiek (2010), under their stated field, hypercharge, Lorentz, color and $SU(2)_L$ conventions, with exact baryon- and lepton-number conservation. The list consists of the source's 15 bosonic, 19 single-fermion-current and 25 four-fermion structures before family multiplicities and Hermitian conjugates; it is not a count of independent three-family complex coefficients. Include all family-index components for three generations, with the source's stated permutation, Hermiticity and conjugation rules; impose no family-universality or diagonal-flavor restriction. No right-handed neutrino field or dimension-five Weinberg operator is included.

In particular, this contract includes the source representative $Q_{H\Box}=(H^\dagger H)\Box(H^\dagger H)$, with $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and the mostly-plus metric of the adopted model. It has canonical dimension six because each Higgs field has dimension one and $\Box$ has dimension two.

For $Q_i^{(6)}$ use the dimensionless Wilson coefficient convention
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dim}\,6}=\frac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\sum_i C_i Q_i^{(6)},\qquad \Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0,$$
with the coefficient tensors chosen so the density is real after the required Hermitian conjugates are added. The retained operator contract has derivative-jet order at most two, maximum field degree six, canonical dimension at most six, and loop order zero. Compactly supported field variations make total divergences vanish in action-level uses.

The source's complete-basis assertion is adopted as a literature-defined coefficient list, not proved by this item. The separate finite invariant-operator quotient supplies only its declared complex-algebraic selection. In this contract that quotient is explicitly formal: no equality between its algebraic invariant space and the full physical compact-gauge invariant space, and no local proof of the EOM/IBP/Fierz classification, is claimed. The mathematical chain used to formulate that finite quotient retains its exact full Axiom of Choice premise.

def-aqft-chiral-power-counting.physical_scope: A source-convention chiral/loop ordering for local electroweak HEFT operators and diagrams through one-loop NLO. It is a formal truncation label, not a convergence proof, numerical uncertainty, coefficient calculation, or physical-validity measurement.

def-aqft-chiral-power-counting:
## Definition

Use the HEFT fields $U$, $h$, gauge curvatures, fermions and arbitrary smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$ from the preceding HEFT model. The canonical engineering dimension $\Delta$ is the mass weight of the local polynomial in fields and derivatives; it is the weight supplied by the finite-jet operator definition. The **chiral/loop count** is separate data and is not inferred from $\Delta$.

Adopt the electroweak chiral loop convention of Buchalla, Catà and Krause. A connected finite diagram has loop number $L\in\mathbb N_0$. Its external lines are counted by $F_L$ left-handed fermions, $F_R$ right-handed fermions, $V$ gauge bosons, $B$ Goldstone bosons, and $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ scalar singlets. In the leading Lagrangian, let $\nu_k$ count Yukawa vertices with $k$ Goldstone legs, $m_l$ gauge-Goldstone vertices with $l$ Goldstone legs, $r_s$ two-gauge-boson vertices with $s$ Goldstone legs, $x$ quartic gauge vertices, $u$ triple-gauge vertices, $z_L,z_R$ left- and right-handed fermion-gauge vertices, $\tau_{tb}$ Yukawa vertices with $t$ Goldstone legs and $b$ scalar legs, and $\omega_q$ scalar-potential vertices with $q$ scalar legs. Set
$$\nu=\sum_k\nu_k+\sum_{t,b}\tau_{tb},\qquad m=\sum_lm_l,\qquad r=\sum_sr_s,\qquad z=z_L+z_R,\qquad \omega=\sum_q\omega_q.$$
For these counts the source chiral degree of the external-momentum factor is
$$d_\chi=2L+2-\frac{F_L+F_R}{2}-V-\nu-m-2r-2x-u-z-2\omega.$$
The factors $(\varphi/v)^B$ and $(h/v)^{H_{\mathrm{ext}}}$ contain any number of Goldstone and singlet fields and do not increase $d_\chi$. Vertices $\varphi^{2j}h^a$ from the leading two-derivative scalar sector likewise carry no additional term in this degree formula. Here $\varphi$ denotes the local Goldstone coordinates defined by $U=\exp(2i\varphi^aT_a/v)$ in its stated coordinate chart. The chiral cutoff and loop cutoff are supplied independently; this contract retains the leading order and the one-loop next-to-leading counterterm classes with $L\leq1$ and $d_\chi\geq0$.

The finite next-to-leading structural classes are $UhD^4$, $X^2Uh$, $XUhD^2$, $\psi^2UhD$, $\psi^2UhD^2$, and $\psi^4Uh$, where $U h$ means any number of $U,U^\dagger,h$ factors, $X_{\mu\nu}$ is a gauge curvature, $D$ is a covariant derivative, and $\psi$ is a fermion. Each class may carry a separate smooth function of $h/v$; the count does not truncate its Taylor series in $h$. No class list or operator-level coefficient relation from a finite canonical-dimension SMEFT basis is identified with this full HEFT list.

The scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$ controlling the derivative expansion and the symmetry-breaking scale $v>0$ are separate supplied mass scales. A condition such as external momentum small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}$ is an applicability assumption only. Chiral order and loop order are formal organizing labels, not convergence claims or numerical bounds on omitted terms.

pthm-aqft-smeft-as-restricted-heft-branc.physical_scope: A conditional field-space and finite-polynomial coefficient map from the selected dimension-six linear Higgs model to a restricted nonlinear HEFT branch on the nonzero-doublet patch. It proves no equality of full operator quotients, no converse, no universal HEFT parametrization, no UV completion, and no empirical realization.

pthm-aqft-smeft-as-restricted-heft-branc:
## Statement

Let $v>0$, let $J=(-v,\infty)$, and use the linearly transforming complex doublet $H$ with hypercharge $Y=1/2$ and the nonlinear fields $h\in J$, $U\in SU(2)$, with the gauge transformations and mostly-plus Minkowski conventions of the two adopted electroweak models. Here $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$ is the second Pauli matrix. Put $e_2=(0,1)^T$, $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, and define
$$\Phi:J\times SU(2)\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\},\qquad \Phi(h,U)=\frac{v+h}{\sqrt2}Ue_2.$$
Then $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto the nonzero-doublet field space. Its inverse is obtained from $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$ and $\Sigma(H)=(\widetilde H,H)$ by
$$h=\sqrt2\rho-v,\qquad U=\frac{\Sigma(H)}{\rho}.$$
It is equivariant for $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$: for $g_L\in SU(2)_L$ and $z\in U(1)_Y$, under $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$ one has $U\mapsto g_LU\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3})^{-1}$ and $h\mapsto h$. The point $H=0$ is excluded; no value of $U$ is assigned there.

For the finite selected SMEFT interaction consisting of the renormalizable terms and the source-defined Warsaw representatives through canonical dimension six, substitute $H=\Phi(h,U)$ and its conjugate into each representative and expand covariant derivatives by the product rule. In the unnormalized radial variable $x=h/v$, every resulting coefficient function multiplying a fixed finite HEFT derivative/Goldstone monomial is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most six. More precisely, after choosing a finite ordered list of the resulting HEFT monomials and a common dimensionally consistent coefficient normalization, the HEFT coefficient tuple is $f=R c$, where $c$ is the finite selected SMEFT coefficient tuple and $R$ is the finite matrix defined by this substitution. Thus its functions and coefficients obey the polynomial and linear-image correlations of this selected branch; they are not freely specifiable smooth HEFT functions. For example, an independent coefficient function $e^x$ is not in the degree-at-most-six polynomial class on any open interval. These radial functions are analytic in $h/v$ before any further field reparametrization.

The canonical-dimension cutoff and the separately defined HEFT chiral/loop grading remain distinct: the substitution does not identify all HEFT classes through a chosen chiral order with the Warsaw list. The result is a conditional statement about the named finite coefficient representatives and their local field substitution, not a proof that a formal algebraic invariant quotient equals the full physical compact-gauge invariant space. It asserts neither that every HEFT lies on this branch nor that every HEFT point has a weakly coupled ultraviolet completion.

ex-aqft-smeft-heft-observable-map.physical_scope: A conditional tree-level calculation for the selected SMEFT coefficient point with only Q_HBox nonzero at dimension six. It derives a local scalar kinetic coefficient and charged-vector coupling in the nonzero-doublet patch; it is not a measurement, general HEFT result, continuum statement, or numerical uncertainty estimate.
